title: Contracts excused from the local-business rule
question: On which contracts was the City’s local-business rule (Administrative Code chapter 14B) waived, and for which departments?
finding: The City’s two posted lists show 108 contracts worth $152.3 million excused from the local-business rule in fiscal 2022-23 and 131 worth $182.7 million in fiscal 2023-24. City Administrator accounts for $125.4 million and Public Health for $106.2 million. 3 of the 239 contracts were also awarded without competition, according to the Supplier Contracts table. The largest is Lystek International Limited (TC63002 PUC Biosolids Mgmt Svc, $15.9 million).
how: Read from the two lists the City posted under the titles "FY 22-23 14B Waivers" and "FY 23-24 14B Waivers": contract number, title, prime award amount, department and start date. The lists do not name the supplier, so it and the purchasing rule are taken from the Supplier Contracts table by contract number.
limits: A waiver of chapter 14B is common where no certified local firm does the work, such as a proprietary system or a statewide lobbyist. The lists give no reason for any waiver and cover two years only. Chapter 14B governs the local business enterprise program, which the budget analyst describes as set up to steer City contracts to small and local businesses; the waiver forms held by the Contract Monitoring Division would give the reasons.
